This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Dallas Love Field Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kdal

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service forecasts and supporting model runs project a sunny day across Dallas with a daytime high near 100°F, consistent with the market’s overwhelming 98.5% implied probability for the 100-101°F bin. Above-average warmth stems from persistent high pressure, light easterly flow, and seasonal late-summer insolation, pushing temperatures several degrees above the 1991-2020 normal high of 93°F. Official observations through mid-afternoon already support readings in the upper 90s, with heat indices elevated by humidity. Minor downward revisions remain possible if late-day cloud build-up or localized showers develop, though current guidance assigns low odds to such outcomes before the daily maximum is recorded.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Current forecasts from the National Weather Service and regional models indicate San Francisco’s September 2 high will settle near 68–72 °F under a persistent marine layer and light pre-frontal drizzle that limits afternoon warming.** This aligns with the market’s overwhelming 98 % implied probability for the 72–73 °F bin, reflecting traders’ assessment of official station data (typically SFO or downtown) amid well-below-normal temperatures driven by onshore flow and cloud cover. Historical September averages hover around 70 °F, but the early-season storm has suppressed readings by 5–10 °F across the Bay Area. A stronger or more prolonged marine intrusion, heavier coastal fog, or faster frontal passage could push the official high into the upper 60s and shift the outcome; conversely, any unexpected afternoon clearing would reinforce the current pricing.

title: Highest temperature in Sao Paulo on September 2?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Sao Paulo-Guarulhos International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=sbgr

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Updated model runs and HKO briefings ahead of the 24-hour window will refine these odds.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent southwest monsoon conditions and below-average rainfall are positioning 33°C as the dominant outcome for Singapore’s maximum temperature on September 3.** The Meteorological Service Singapore’s September 1 advisory notes that dry, occasionally windy southeasterly or southwesterly flow will continue, delivering fair skies and strong daytime heating with only isolated late-day showers possible. This setup favors peak temperatures in the 33–35 °C range on most days of the fortnight, consistent with the current model consensus showing afternoon highs near 32–33 °C (89–90 °F) under mostly sunny conditions and light winds.

Climatologically, September averages a daily maximum of 31.6 °C; the current dry spell elevates this baseline by limiting cloud cover and surface moisture. Short-range guidance (including GFS and local runs) shows limited model spread, with the majority clustering around 32–33 °C and only a small tail reaching 34 °C under the clearest, least-ventilated scenarios. The market’s heavy weighting on 33 °C (76 %) therefore reflects the convergence of official agency guidance, recent dry-weather persistence, and low precipitation probabilities that reduce evaporative cooling. Traders appear to assign minimal odds to extremes outside this narrow window given the stability of the monsoon pattern through the next 24–48 hours.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent forecast guidance from global models like GFS and local European sources points to a maximum temperature of 23–24 °C in Warsaw on September 3, 2026, under partly cloudy skies with light westerly flow.** 

Daytime heating will be tempered by increasing cloud cover (40–60 % in many runs) and a modest chance of light showers or drizzle, which limits surface warming. Westerly winds of 2–4 m/s promote mixing that prevents stronger temperature rises, while surface pressure near 1017 hPa supports stable conditions without strong subsidence. Ensemble spreads and hourly profiles from sources such as Yr and GFS-based outputs cluster between 22–24 °C, with afternoon peaks most often near 22–23 °C before cooling begins after 17:00 local time. This narrow range explains the nearly even market-implied odds between the two leading outcomes, as small differences in cloud timing or boundary-layer moisture can shift the daily maximum by 1 °C. Historical September maxima average lower, so current guidance reflects a modest warm anomaly driven by the synoptic pattern rather than extreme heat. Updated model runs and official observations from the Polish Institute of Meteorology will provide the final resolution data.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent rain and extensive cloud cover tied to a low-pressure system and Tropical Storm Saudel's outer circulation are the dominant factors capping daytime heating in Taipei on September 4. eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and model guidance indicate a typical late-summer subtropical pattern over Houston, with light southeast winds, high boundary-layer moisture, and afternoon convective development expected to cap surface heating on September 4. Scattered showers and thunderstorms, driven by diurnal instability and possible sea-breeze interactions, are forecast to develop by midday, limiting insolation and preventing temperatures from climbing into the mid-90s. Ensemble consensus and historical analogs for early-September days with similar moisture profiles and weak steering flow point to a daily maximum most often between 88–92 °F. Market-implied odds cluster tightly around 88–91 °F because traders weigh the uncertain timing and coverage of convection against the modest climatological average high near 91 °F; any delay in storm initiation or reduced cloud cover could shift the outcome toward the upper end of that range before resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=ksfo

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This pattern suppresses temperatures 5–10°F below the long-term September average of about 70°F by enhancing the marine layer and westerly winds that moderate coastal conditions. Trader consensus favoring 68–71°F bins reflects model agreement on post-storm moderation without strong warming, alongside historical precedent for mild early-September days when marine influence dominates. Updated model runs and any shifts in wind patterns ahead of resolution will likely drive further adjustments in implied probabilities.
